title: The Soul Is Always Praying
hook: Rav Kook wrote of the soul's longing for the infinite
tomorrow: what changes when you say "you" instead of "it"?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Rav Kook's hope for a gentler world, a kindness wide enough to reach the animals: gentleness to all. Same rabbi today, looking inward this time.

One in the morning. A browser tab that never gets closed: a summer theater program in New York, photos of a black stage, a deadline in red. Noa has read the page so many times she could perform it. She types to a friend, then deletes it, then types it again: i don't even know what i want from it. Some wants come with a name and a price. Others just ache, and the thing on the screen is only where the ache landed tonight. A rabbi in Jerusalem, Abraham Isaac Kook, wrote a great deal about that second kind. He didn't treat it as a problem.
screen: `ONE A.M., ONE TAB STILL OPEN.` → `I DON'T EVEN KNOW WHAT I WANT.` → `SOME WANTS JUST ACHE.`

segments.voice: Rav Kook taught that the soul is always praying. Not only in synagogue, not only when words come out: underneath everything, it keeps reaching toward its source, the infinite, the way a flame keeps leaning up. In his telling, the prayers in the prayer book are the moments that hidden prayer finally becomes audible. That's the fact to repeat tonight: for Kook, prayer doesn't start the longing. It lets you hear the longing that was already going. He was reading an old picture. Proverbs says, "The spirit of man is the lamp of the LORD." And a psalm says it outright: "My soul yearneth, yea, even pineth for the courts of the LORD." So what does that do with a one a.m. ache? Kook doesn't tell anyone to crush it, and he doesn't say every want is holy either. He suggests listening underneath. A wish for a stage, a city, a person can be a small window onto a larger reach, the soul's pull toward something without an edge. The program may be right or wrong for Noa. The longing itself isn't a mistake. It might be a prayer, and an honest one.
screen: `THE SOUL IS ALWAYS PRAYING.` · `PRAYER MAKES THE LONGING AUDIBLE.` · `THE LAMP OF THE LORD.` · `LISTEN UNDER THE WANT.` · then, large: `THE SOUL LONGS.`

segments.voice: Close your eyes and let one longing come up, the one that keeps showing up late at night. Don't solve it and don't argue with it. Sit beside it, and ask it gently what it's reaching for underneath.
screen: `ONE LONGING.` · `SIT BESIDE IT.` · `WHAT IS IT REACHING FOR?`

segments.voice: The soul longs: Rav Kook's teaching that the soul reaches, without pause, toward its source, and that prayer is that reach said out loud.
Pocket this: the soul is always praying. In Kook's telling, the ache is already a kind of prayer.

howItsDone: Rav Kook's writings on the soul's longing and on prayer are studied in many yeshivot and adult classes, and his idea that the soul is always praying is often taught alongside the prayer book.

chat.meaning: Rav Kook taught the soul is always reaching toward its source. A want can be a window onto that reach, worth listening under, not crushing or obeying blindly.

tie.story: Rav Kook taught that the soul is always praying, reaching toward its source, and spoken prayer lets that hidden prayer be heard.
tie.friend: Noa's 1 a.m. ache over the program may be her soul reaching; she can listen under it before she decides.
tie.you: what is your own longing reaching for?
